title: Universal integer termination of affine linear loops
formal: Is there a deterministic Turing machine that always halts and decides universal integer termination of every affine loop \[\text{while }Bx\ge c\text{ do }x:=Ax+a,\] where \(A\in\mathbb Z^{d\times d}\), \(a\in\mathbb Z^d\), \(B\in\mathbb Z^{m\times d}\) and \(c\in\mathbb Z^m\) are explicit finite input data, \(d,m\ge1\), and the inequality is componentwise? More precisely, with \(f(x)=Ax+a\), decide whether \[\forall x_0\in\mathbb Z^d\ \exists n\in\mathbb N\ \exists i\in\{1,\ldots,m\},\qquad (Bf^n(x_0))_i<c_i.\] There is no diagonalizability restriction on \(A\). The answer is affirmative by the 2019 theorem cited below; this card records the resolved historical question.
why: Universal termination is a basic verification question about a program before its inputs are known. The affine class isolates a substantial decidable fragment despite infinitely many states and arbitrary repeated eigenvalues. Its resolution also demonstrates that quantifying over all initial states can have a different algorithmic status from deciding the behavior of one supplied trajectory.
status_note: Resolved by Hosseini, Ouaknine and Worrell, ICALP 2019, §5 Theorem 16. The checked theorem covers arbitrary integer affine updates and finite conjunctions of affine guards; strict/non-strict forms translate exactly over integer states. The 24 July 2026 survey restates the result. Archived after matching the source target to the published resolution; no independent Lean formalization of the paper is claimed.
review_note: Completed individual review against P versus NP on 2026-09-16; see research/card-completion-20260913/reviews.jsonl.

progress.text: The survey records universal termination algorithms over real and rational initial states. The corresponding integer affine problem remained distinct.
The original source records integer decidability for diagonalizable updates, while leaving arbitrary affine update matrices open.
Hosseini, Ouaknine and Worrell publish Theorem 16 at ICALP: universal integer termination is decidable for all single-path affine loops with finitely many affine guard inequalities.
The revised survey states the general decidability result in Theorem 3.5 and distinguishes the still-open fixed-initial-state problem.
Individual review checked the original guard convention against the final 2019 multiple-guard theorem. The unrestricted historical target is resolved and archived.

importance.reason: A major historical decidability question for an elementary and widely used infinite-state program model. The unrestricted integer affine case removed the remaining general-matrix restriction and clarified the boundary with fixed-initial-state positivity; now resolved, so it is not retained as an open benchmark.

sentences: An affine linear loop repeatedly applies an integer matrix update and translation while all of its linear guard inequalities hold.
Universal integer termination asks whether every integer initial vector eventually violates at least one guard, with a stopping time that may depend on the vector.
The historical question removed the diagonalizability assumption and allowed arbitrary dimensions and repeated eigenvalue blocks.
Hosseini, Ouaknine and Worrell proved the full decision problem decidable in 2019, including conjunctions of guards.
The card is therefore archived as resolved, while the separate question of termination from one supplied initial vector remains outside this result.

definitions: The state is an unbounded integer column vector, with exact arithmetic and no overflow or rounding. At each iteration the entire conjunction \(Bx\ge c\) is tested; a failed inequality exits immediately, and otherwise all coordinates are simultaneously replaced by \(Ax+a\). The only control path uses this same update at every iteration. Let \(\mathbb N=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}\), \(f^0(x)=x\), and \(f^{n+1}(x)=f(f^n(x))\). In the displayed predicate the iterates are defined even after a guard fails; the first failing iterate specifies the actual loop's termination. Thus \(n=0\) includes starts outside the guard. All entries are signed binary integers, and dimensions and finite row lists are explicitly encoded; malformed descriptions may be rejected. Both dimensions and all coefficient sizes are unrestricted input parameters. Every integer initial vector is quantified, including vectors not satisfying the guard. The stopping iteration may depend on the initial vector; no common stopping-time bound is requested. The algorithm receives the loop, not an initial-state restriction. The affine translation and guard constants may be nonzero, and repeated eigenvalues and arbitrary Jordan blocks are allowed. The question requires one uniform error-free total machine with no oracle or prescribed running-time bound.
answer_criterion: A complete Lean-checked proof of the affirmative decidability theorem must specify a total computable procedure that correctly classifies every loop in this exact input model. Its yes-answer means that every integer start terminates; its no-answer means that at least one integer start runs forever. A theorem for real starts, rational starts, homogeneous loops or diagonalizable updates alone does not meet this criterion. Neither an algorithm for a supplied initial state nor a uniform bound on all terminating runs is required. The published resolution is the reason for archival; this review does not claim that its proof has already been formalized in Lean.

source_formulation.text: Determine whether termination from every integer initial state is decidable for general affine linear loops, without assuming the update matrix is diagonalizable.
source_formulation.caption: Editorial paraphrase of the historical open question

context_blocks.text: The loop has one deterministic update but infinitely many possible inputs. Universal termination permits different inputs to take different numbers of iterations. For example, decrementing a positive integer eventually exits for every integer start, although the number of iterations is unbounded as the starting value grows.

The 2015 survey distinguishes termination over all integer states from termination at one fixed integer state. It presents positive results for diagonalizable update matrices and records the unrestricted integer affine case as open. Nonzero translations matter because homogenizing an affine map introduces a distinguished extra coordinate; quantifying over all values of that coordinate changes the initial-state domain.

The 2019 paper proves the full general case. Its §5 explicitly handles conjunctions of guards, and Theorem 16 states the decision procedure for arbitrary update matrices. The paper writes strict guards \(g_i(x)>0\); the present source convention \((Bx)_i\ge c_i\) is exactly equivalent on integer states to \((Bx)_i-c_i+1>0\). This translation preserves every run and does not impose any spectral assumption.

This match is stronger than a title or abstract comparison: the checked final section permits arbitrarily many guards with a shared affine update. The theorem decides the existence of an integer nonterminating start and hence its complement, universal termination. A statement limited to one guard would not alone justify removing a card whose source allows a conjunction.

The July 2026 survey again states decidability for affine single-path loops over integers. It separately retains the difficulty of a supplied initial state, where positivity of a particular recurrence sequence is relevant. The present archival therefore does not resolve Positivity or Ultimate Positivity, and it does not settle general loops whose next state is specified by a nondeterministic relation.
